recipes.name: Court's Creamy and Quick Burritos
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of mushroom soup

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Cook ground beef and onion in a skillet over medium heat until beef is completely browned, 7 to 10 minutes. Drain excess grease from the skillet. Stir 1 cup Cheddar cheese, refried beans, and taco seasoning into ground beef; set aside.
Combine soup, sour cream, and salsa in a bowl; spread about ½ into the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish. Set aside.

Spoon beef mixture down center of each tortilla; roll tortillas around filling. Arrange rolled tortillas in a single layer in the baking dish, seam-sides down. Pour remaining ½ soup mixture over tortillas. Top with remaining 1 ½ cups Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until cheese is bubbly and melted, 30 to 35 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Court's Creamy and Quick Burritos
raw_recipe.description: Court's creamy and quick burritos is a simple recipe for six beef burritos topped with creamy Cheddar cheese, mushroom soup, and sour cream sauce.

review.reviewBody: My family really loved this recipe!! Even my 4,5,&,6 year olds liked it!! It was easy too. The flavors were a bit flat though. I don't know why because the taco packet, salsa, and cream soup are flavored. Prob would make again:), but would add cilantro, or maybe Swiss cheese! Mmmmmm

This was great with the following changes: To the ground beef add; 2 tsp of Cumin powder and Ancho Chili Powder along with the taco seasoning packet. Chopped garlic is a must and I used about a Tbsp and a handful of fresh cilantro and a chopped bell pepper. To the sauce; I used one 7oz can of Salsa Ranchero plus approx 1/4 Cup of Picante. Without these changes the recipe would have been bland.

This was so much better than I expected! I generally avoid using "cream of" soups. I was in a rush so I used cream of chicken (cream of mushroom isn't my favorite) and it worked out quite well. In the future, I'd probably make my own cream sauce with crema, beef stock, and some cumin, then thicken a bit with a roux. However, on the quick, cream of whatever works well. It had a lot of flavor and even the kids ate it-- and had seconds! (A minor miracle...). Would also be great using chicken or piccadillo.

I thought this was really good! I had shredded beef I cooked in my crockpot and wanted to make an enchilada type dish but lacked tomato paste or chile powder. I was skeptical using a cream of chicken in a Mexican dish ! But wow it was yummy! My roommate isn’t a fan of refried beans, so I cooked white rice and added pico de gallo and salsa with the shredded beef, rolled in four tortillas and rolled them in the sauce covered with cheese and topped with sliced black olives. Delish! Will make this again.

This is very similar to a recipe by Deanna House from Kalamazoo Michigan. I leave the salsa as a topping after the casserole is done. I recommend adding a 4oz can of green chilies to the sour cream/soup mix. My favorite comfort food!

I made this for my husband and I last night and it was delicious! I changed the 1/2 cup salsa to 1/4 cup salsa + 1/4 cup hot taco sauce. I used black bean refried beans with roasted red jalapenos and a hot and spicy taco seasoning. I also used light sour cream instead of regular sour cream and it still came out perfect. Then on top of the cheese I added some chipotle seasoning. It gave it the perfect amount of spice and lots of flavor. It seems like this is a good recipe to play around with and add whatever you like. I will definitely make these again!

This is very good. It made a lot more than 6 though, which is a good thing. (Maybe my tortillas were smaller than 9") I made about 9 burritos and still had a little bit of meat left over, so I put it on top of the burritos before adding the sauce and cheese. I did sub black beans for the refried beans. Add some coleslaw and you've got an easy-to-make weeknight dinner.

Great! I only made two changes--cream of chicken instead of cream of mushroom soup, and less cheese on top. My picky eater (3.5 years old) didn't care for it, but my 5 and 1 year olds gobbled it up. My hubby loved it and had to resist after his third or so helping. :D Thank you for sharing!
We loved this! I subbed black beans for the refried beans (what I had in the pantry) and it was really good! I bet refried beans would be delicious as well! I've already made this recipe twice!
Absolutely delicious and easy to make. Highly recommended.

I would have given this four stars but I omitted the soup. My family prefers it that way. In addition, if adding soup and baking it becomes an enchilada. All of the ingredients except for the soup is the way I typically make a fast ground beef filling for burritos. Throw the tortillas over the gas flame for a few seconds each and serve with sour cream and salsa on the side.
These burritos were simply amazing. Real easy to make & taste great. Definitely will be a part of our menu.
Yum! Add salsa on top for extra spice and freshness.
These turned out very tasty, and made good leftovers too!
The whole family loved it, the only thing I changed was that I added chopped green chilis in the sauce, a huge hit and will be making it again
I used corn tortillas and it was very tasty!! Kiddos enjoyed it very much, as they had 2nd's & 3rd's. This is a keeper and I'll definitely be making again.
The burritos were super soggy and mushy. I did not enjoy this recipe at all. I only gave it a 2 because it was quick.
